<reason>Both sides fought a genuinely tight, well-structured debate on the agreed metric (deaths by 2030), and both answered pressure questions in the required A1/A2 format. The debate turned on two exchanges. First, B's Q1 forced A to abandon price/scarcity as the transmission mechanism for interdiction. That concession was costly because A had earlier explicitly routed both of its forward-looking claims — suppressed initiation and reduced purchasing by current users [A2.6] — through price. A's substitute mechanism ("tonnage removed, networks broken," plus a vague claim of spot shortages) is thinner, and B's closing crystallized this precisely: pull price out and what remains is activity, not scarcity. B's companion charge that A's theory is unfalsifiable (rising deaths = "restructuring," falling deaths = "pressure caught up") was never squarely answered. Second, A's strongest live route — the opt-in coverage wall, four in five untreated, and the vivid point that naloxone cannot be self-administered by someone using alone — did real damage and A pressed it well in closing. But B answered it plausibly by shifting from "the patient won't come" to "the door is the problem" (take-homes, telehealth induction, pharmacy/ER/jail initiation, vans), and by noting that a seizure in Arizona reaches that solitary user even less than a neighbor's kit does. B also gave the better discontinuity story for the 2024 bend — settlement money landing near-simultaneously plus a nonlinear naloxone-density threshold and east-to-west geographic pattern — which met A's own falsifiability test better than A's answer met B's. A's rebuttal that fentanyl kills the newly exposed within months was a good repair of the five-year clock objection, and its retention/postponement arguments were sharp, but the self-inflicted mechanism gap left A's "whole-market intervention" claim resting on availability effects it had just conceded could not be observed. B made the choice easier to decide.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Q1 demanding a price or purity signal, followed by A's admission that "pressure cannot transmit through price," which B then converted in closing into the observation that price was the load-bearing beam of A's initiation-suppression and reduced-consumption arguments — paired with the unanswered charge that A's supply story fits every outcome and therefore predicts none.</best_rebuttal>
